Polygonize a raster, one polygon per cell

Source: R/polygonize.R
polygonize_raster.Rd

Turns each cell of a one-layer raster that has a value into a square polygon holding that value, such as the planning-unit polygons of an AOI raster from rasterize_aoi(). Neighbouring cells with the same value stay separate polygons, so every cell keeps its own row.

Usage

polygonize_raster(x, value = names(x), id = NULL)

Arguments

x

The raster: a SpatRaster with one layer, or a path to a raster file with one layer.

value

The name of the column that holds each cell's raster value: a single, non-empty string. Defaults to the layer's name ("index" for the default output of rasterize_aoi()). wtw-data-prep2 uses "NCCID".

id

NULL (the default) or the name of a column to add that numbers the polygons 1 to n in their order (see "Method"): a single, non-empty string, different from value. wtw-data-prep2 uses "PUID".

Value

An sf data frame with one POLYGON row per cell that has a value, in the raster's CRS, with the columns value (the cell's value, an integer or a double as the raster stores it), then id (an integer, 1 to n) if given, then geometry. A raster with no values gives zero rows. Nothing is written.

Method

  • Polygons: terra::as.polygons() with dissolve = FALSE. Each cell that is not NA becomes one square polygon whose corners are the cell's corners (a ring of four corners, closed), so polygons share edges exactly with their neighbours. Neighbouring cells with equal values are not merged. Cells that are NA get no polygon.

  • Order: terra's cell order, row by row from the top-left cell, so id 1 is the first cell with a value in the top row that has one. The order does not depend on the values.

  • Values: each cell's value, not rounded, in the type the raster stores (ADR 0019): an integer column if the raster stores integers (terra::is.int(): an INT* data type on file, such as NAT_DATA's idx.tif, or integer values in memory, such as the cell numbers of rasterize_aoi()), and a double column if it stores floats, even when the values are whole numbers. Integers outside R's integer range (possible only with INT4U or larger types) stay doubles. Files written from the result keep the type, so a shapefile gets an integer field.

  • CRS: the raster's; nothing is reprojected and no areas are computed.

Every cell with a value becomes a polygon, so polygonizing a large raster (such as the whole national template) makes millions of polygons; crop the raster to the area first, as rasterize_aoi() does by default.

See also

rasterize_aoi() makes the AOI rasters this function is used on.

Other raster: align_raster(), write_rasters()

Examples

template <- system.file("extdata", "template.tif", package = "constechr")
aoi <- system.file("extdata", "aoi.gpkg", package = "constechr")
x <- rasterize_aoi(aoi, template, cells = "touches")

# One polygon per cell, holding its template cell number in "index"
polygonize_raster(x)
#> Simple feature collection with 9 features and 1 field
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1003000 ymin: 604000 xmax: 1006000 ymax: 607000
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>   index                       geometry
#> 1    34 POLYGON ((1003000 606000, 1...
#> 2    35 POLYGON ((1004000 606000, 1...
#> 3    36 POLYGON ((1005000 606000, 1...
#> 4    44 POLYGON ((1003000 605000, 1...
#> 5    45 POLYGON ((1004000 605000, 1...
#> 6    46 POLYGON ((1005000 605000, 1...
#> 7    54 POLYGON ((1003000 604000, 1...
#> 8    55 POLYGON ((1004000 604000, 1...
#> 9    56 POLYGON ((1005000 604000, 1...

# wtw-data-prep2's column names, with planning units numbered 1 to n
pu <- polygonize_raster(x, value = "NCCID", id = "PUID")
pu
#> Simple feature collection with 9 features and 2 fields
#> Geometry type: POLYGON
#> Dimension:     XY
#> Bounding box:  xmin: 1003000 ymin: 604000 xmax: 1006000 ymax: 607000
#> Projected CRS: Canada_Albers_WGS_1984
#>   NCCID PUID                       geometry
#> 1    34    1 POLYGON ((1003000 606000, 1...
#> 2    35    2 POLYGON ((1004000 606000, 1...
#> 3    36    3 POLYGON ((1005000 606000, 1...
#> 4    44    4 POLYGON ((1003000 605000, 1...
#> 5    45    5 POLYGON ((1004000 605000, 1...
#> 6    46    6 POLYGON ((1005000 605000, 1...
#> 7    54    7 POLYGON ((1003000 604000, 1...
#> 8    55    8 POLYGON ((1004000 604000, 1...
#> 9    56    9 POLYGON ((1005000 604000, 1...

# Equal values are not merged: nine cells of 1 give nine polygons
ones <- rasterize_aoi(aoi, template, cells = "touches", value = 1)
nrow(polygonize_raster(ones))
#> [1] 9
